chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man against whom three testified that he had committed adultery with so-and-so, and the fourth testified that he did not know with whom he had committed adultery. He said: 'He is neither whipped nor stoned.'

key_terms.رجم: stoning (a form of corporal punishment for married adulterers)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on adultery punishment when one of four witnesses is unsure about the identity of the woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of 'shubha' (doubt) in hadd punishments, where uncertainty in a key element of testimony prevents the full application of the penalty. It highlights the rigorous evidentiary standards required for stoning (rajm) and whipping (jald), emphasizing that even a single witness's doubt regarding the specific partner can nullify the collective testimony. This ruling underscores the precautionary approach in Shia fiqh to avoid imposing severe corporal punishments on the basis of ambiguous evidence.
